findings.description: Policy tests assert literal production Markdown phrases rather than observable inventory or workflow behaviour.
findings.analysis: These assertions can pass for contradictory guidance and fail during harmless wording edits. They do not validate decision-gated lifecycle behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Remove literal prose assertions. Retain actual inventory/index coverage and defer behavioural lifecycle validation to the separate deterministic validator change.
findings.rationale: Literal documentation assertions are not reliable behavioural validation and conflict with the project's testing approach.

findings.description: Decision-gated estimates for a named queued spec can hand planning to the active spec.
findings.analysis: The decision-gated handoff must preserve an explicitly selected target. Otherwise a queued change can cause design or tasks artifacts to be written to the unrelated active change.
findings.recommendation: Accept. Preserve the selected target through automatic planning handoffs.
findings.rationale: Every automatic handoff should explicitly retain its selected target, regardless of the target's kind; active-spec defaults remain only for unnamed direct invocations.

findings.description: Prepared bugfix/refactor and revise workflows stop before an unambiguous decision-gated continuation.
findings.analysis: This conflicts with the selected decision-gated policy: a successful abbreviated implementation should progress to verification, and a revision should proceed through its applicable planning stage when no decision remains.
findings.recommendation: Accept. Add policy-aware continuation while preserving manual-mode handoffs.
findings.rationale: Decision-gated progression should continue through unambiguous abbreviated-work and revision transitions while manual mode remains explicitly user-driven.

findings.description: Automatic downstream handoffs omit a named non-active target.
findings.analysis: Named non-active work cannot safely rely on a downstream skill's active-spec default. The name must travel through verify, review, and triage.
findings.recommendation: Accept. Carry the selected target through every automatic handoff.
findings.rationale: All automatic handoffs retain their selected spec name, irrespective of kind or active status.

findings.description: The spec workflow itself does not continue automatically into planning.
findings.analysis: A completed feature specification normally has an unambiguous next planning stage. This is part of decision-gated progression rather than a new workflow.
findings.recommendation: Vary. Keep spec strictly planning-only and add an explicit activation boundary.
findings.rationale: Spec creates requirements and a brief only; it must never select itself as the current issue or auto-progress. A new activate <spec-name> skill explicitly selects a queued normal spec, then immediately invokes its next planning stage regardless of the project's progression mode.

findings.description: Prepared independent work is blocked while another unrelated spec is active.
findings.analysis: The project deliberately avoids executing unrelated prepared work in a shared worktree. Such work should be undertaken separately, not relaxed into the current workflow.
findings.recommendation: Decline. The current guard preserves separation of concerns; separate-worktree support is future work.
findings.rationale: Bugfixes and refactors are sidecar fast-track work that normally unblocks delivery of the current item; unrelated work belongs in a separate worktree.

findings.description: Concurrent build invocations could race when updating task progress.
findings.analysis: The finding assumes concurrent agents operating the same spec in one worktree. Atomic task claiming is a broader concurrency design and is outside this policy change.
findings.recommendation: Decline. Do not introduce speculative locking or state-merge machinery here.
findings.rationale: The workflow does not support concurrent build invocations for the same spec in one worktree; no speculative concurrency machinery is warranted.

findings.description: Completed parent tasks have unchecked sub-items in the delivered task plan.
findings.analysis: The recorded completed task plan should agree with verification evidence and status.
findings.recommendation: Accept. Mark implemented sub-items complete after confirming the plan reflects delivered work.
findings.rationale: The implementation is complete; task detail must accurately reflect the delivered work and verification record.

findings.description: Runtime context still advertises the removed implement skill.
findings.analysis: The active-skills context snapshot must match the installed inventory or it can direct an agent to an unavailable workflow.
findings.recommendation: Accept. Remove implement from the context skill inventory.
findings.rationale: Runtime context must accurately represent the installed skill inventory.

findings.description: A forced installation might leave an obsolete removed skill in an existing target.
findings.analysis: The existing specle_group frontmatter is the management marker. During a forced installation, directories with that marker that are absent from the incoming inventory are obsolete managed skills and must be removed safely; unmarked skills remain untouched.
findings.recommendation: Accept. Stage the new distribution, recoverably remove obsolete marked skill directories, install replacements and the index, and restore all backups on failure.
findings.rationale: A forced installation must synchronise the managed inventory, including removal of obsolete specle_group-marked skills, without affecting unrelated skills.
